demographics.note: Zernio’s public API does not expose audience demographics (age, gender, location) for LinkedIn. The audience section below therefore only shows what the platform itself publishes.

audienceFit.why: Heads of department, placement cells, registrars and edtech buyers are all here — and education is LinkedIn's highest-engagement industry.

diagnosis.headline: The funnel is working end to end: 1 published → 5.4K impressions → 279 engagement → 88 clicks. Now scale what already works.

benchmark.typical: 3.9% average · 3.0–4.0% for education (highest of any industry)
benchmark.reference: Published 2026 industry benchmarks (Hootsuite, Socialinsider, Quid/Rival IQ, SociaVault) — a reference range, not your data.
benchmark.note: Document/carousel posts lead at ≈7% engagement. Dwell time and comments in the first hour decide distribution; a bare external link suppresses reach, so put links in the first comment.

actions.title: Scale the format that produced this
actions.detail: Repeat the top-performing item's structure for universities and departments and put a small budget or a partner share behind it.

diagnosis.mechanics: Text-with-image and document/carousel posts get the most dwell time. Post from a personal profile, tag the institution, and put any external link in the first comment.

audienceFit.why: Resource and lesson-planning searches exist, but institutions do not buy from Pinterest.

diagnosis.headline: The funnel is working end to end: 3 published → 23.7K impressions → 553 engagement → 92 outboundClicks. Now scale what already works.

zeros.label: Closeups
zeros.explanation: No closeups on any of the 3 post(s) read in this range (they recorded 553 other interaction(s) between them), and the account-level closeups insight is empty too. This is a measured zero, not a missing metric.

benchmark.reference: Published 2026 industry benchmarks (Hootsuite, Socialinsider, Quid/Rival IQ, SociaVault) — a reference range, not your data.
benchmark.note: Pins are indexed like search results, not like a feed. A fresh pin usually takes 2–4 weeks before impressions appear, and it can keep driving traffic for months. Keywords in the pin title and board name do the targeting.

actions.title: Scale the format that produced this
actions.detail: Repeat the top-performing item's structure for universities and departments and put a small budget or a partner share behind it.

diagnosis.mechanics: Keyword-rich pin titles, vertical 2:3 creative, and boards named for what an institution would search ("college attendance tracking", "campus management"). Volume and consistency beat virality.
